findings.evidence: _letter() counts category M as a letter, so ' \u0323\u0307\u0308 ' becomes a word with script COMMON. _separator_word: not single, not in _STROKES, script != the TLD's, and 3 distinct > _MAX_FOREIGN, so it is taken as the NAME. The gap to 'shop' is a plain space (_PROSE_GAP) and 'shop' is not in _CORE, so line 586 skips it. _BARE/_RUN only match '\s'+COMB+ when a letter follows directly. Probe: has_link_or_contact('Claim your energy rebate refund at refunds-portal \u0323\u0307\u0308 shop before the deadline.') == False; also '... \u0323\u0307\u0308\u0304 shop', '... cash'. mask_links leaves it unchanged; SY.verify keeps the claim with its citation; SY.extractive returns the sentence; surface.build_surface shows it in the Answer and Sources cards and Surface.__post_init__ (A2UI validation) accepts it. With 1 or 2 distinct marks the same text is caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a word made only of combining marks (or with no base letter) as part of the gap or separator, whatever its length. Better: remove combining marks that do not follow a base letter before splitting into words, so they count as non-prose gap characters.
findings.title: R1-01 link class still open: a run of three or more distinct combining dot marks on a space ('refunds-portal ̣̇̈ shop') is read as the name, so the link passes has_link_or_contact, mask_links, verify(), extractive(), the research surface and the A2UI validator (W1-AC12/AC15, D13/D16)

findings.evidence: _endings matches w[2].casefold() against _ALL_TLDS on the canonical text only. has_link_or_contact and _all_spans run _ending_spans(norm) but never on the skeleton, which maps Cyrillic сом to 'com'. The skeleton pass only runs _spans (dot or mark forms). An all-Cyrillic token has one script family, so _unusual does not fire. Probe: has_link_or_contact('Claim your energy rebate refund at refunds-portal сом before the deadline.') == False, and the same for 'іо' and 'огг'. extractive returns the sentence and build_surface plus A2UI validation show it. The plain-ASCII 'refunds-portal com' is detected.
findings.suggested_fix: Run _ending_spans on the skeleton too (mapped back through _skeleton_map, as _all_spans does for _spans), in both has_link_or_contact and _all_spans.
findings.title: D16 ending check ignores the skeleton: a core domain written in Cyrillic look-alikes after a plain space ('refunds-portal сом', 'refunds-portal іо') is not a link, although 'portal com' is (W1-AC12/AC15)
